content_preview.title: Microsoft Says Windows Updates From October 13 Might Leave SQL Server Linked-Server Connections Open; Fix Promised, Sources Differ on Windows 11 26H2
content_preview.summary: Microsoft's release-health pages say Windows updates released October 13, 2026 might leave SQL Server linked server connections open, with Oracle and PostgreSQL among those known to be affected; The Register differs from a Microsoft page on 26H2.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft has confirmed a known issue in which, after Windows updates released October 13, 2026 are installed, connections created by SQL Server linked server queries "might remain open after the queries complete," according to its [Windows Server 2025 release-health page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-health/status-windows-server-2025). The page lists the issue as Confirmed and says it was opened at 15:11 PT on 2026-11-11. On the same [release-health page](https...

editor_notes.content_quality: News, 849 words (range 400-1200), 149-character title (limit 150). Clear structure: lead, what Microsoft's pages say, per-release KB mapping, the 26H2 discrepancy, what is not known. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference, no causal claims beyond Microsoft's text (the article repeats only Microsoft's wording that OLE DB providers are involved and that Oracle and PostgreSQL connections are 'among those known to be affected'; it names no other database or cause and explicitly says other targets are neither named nor excluded). Databases-area check: SQL Server, Oracle and PostgreSQL appear only as Microsoft names them.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 10 snapshots read from disk (sources/2026-11/<slug>/source-0..9.html.gz; manifest: all HTTP 200, source-8 BleepingComputer via Archive.org fallback because the live fetch was bot-checked, suspicious_patterns null for every source, so no prompt-injection scan hits to judge). Snapshots extracted to text and every quoted string in the article (13 quote strings) was machine-matched against the pages it is attributed to: all found verbatim. HEADLINE: (a) 'Microsoft Says': all eight Microsoft pages carry the entry 'SQL Server linked server connections might remain open', status Confirmed, Opened 2026-11-11 15:11 PT (source-0..7). (b) 'Windows Updates From October 13': each page says 'After Windows updates released October 13, 2026 (KB...), and later are installed on server devices'; originating-update date column 2026-10-13 on all eight; KBs recomputed from the snapshots: Server 2025 KB5126646 (build 26100.33650), Server 2022 KB5126655, Win10 1809/Server 2019 KB5126651, Server 2012 KB5126835, Win11 24H2/25H2/26H2 KB5127648, Win11 26H1 KB5127646 - all match the article's mapping. 2026-10-13 is the second Tuesday of October 2026 (Patch Tuesday), so it is the release date. (c) 'Might Leave ... Connections Open': Microsoft's wording is 'might remain open after the queries complete' (headline keeps the qualifier; the later 'can accumulate' is Microsoft's own wording for accumulation and the article quotes it as such); OLE DB providers, Oracle and PostgreSQL named as 'among those known to be affected'. (d) 'Fix Promised': 'Next steps: We will address this issue with an out-of-band update that will be released in the next few days. We will update this documentation once the update is released.' on all eight pages, last updated 2026-11-11 15:37 PT (26H2: 2026-11-12 10:50 PT). RE-CHECK NOW (2026-11-13 ~09:58 UTC): all eight pages re-fetched live and their sha256 equal the manifest hashes, i.e. byte-identical to the snapshots: still Confirmed, no fix released, so the article's statement that each page still showed Confirmed with the same text is accurate. (e) 'Sources Differ on Windows 11 26H2': affected-platform lists recounted by script: the 26H2 page lists 13 platforms (7 client incl. Windows 11 26H2, 6 server); the other seven cited pages list 12 (6 client, 6 server) without 26H2 - the article's 13 vs 12 is correct. The Register (Richard Speed, 'Published thu 12 Nov 2026 // 12:06 UTC', meta published_time 2026-11-12T12:06:04Z, article:modified_time empty) says 'According to Microsoft, the technical glitch affects every version of Windows except Windows 11 26H2, stretching back to Windows 10 1809 and LTSC 2019, and Windows Server from 2025 back to 2012' - verbatim. The live Register page is byte-identical to the snapshot (no correction, no update note). 12:06 UTC = 04:06 PST (UTC-8; DST ended 2026-11-01), correct and correctly labelled PT. The 26H2 entry's Last updated 2026-11-12 10:50 PT (18:50 UTC) is 6h44m AFTER the Register's publication, while the other pages' 2026-11-11 15:37 PT is before it. No third source explains the difference: Archive.org has no capture of the 26H2 page between 2026-11-09 and now, and the pages carry no change note, so the article's statement that no cited source explains the difference or says the page was edited afterwards is accurate. 'Differ' is therefore a fair description of the two sources as fetched, but the article leaves the timing inference implicit - see clarification. BleepingComputer (Sergiu Gatlan, November 12, 2026; live page shows 07:11 AM): 'Microsoft Says Windows updates ... impact both client (Windows 10 and Windows 11) and server (Windows Server 2012 and later) systems and will be fixed with an out-of-band Windows update to be released over the next few days'; the 'Wednesday' dashboard update = 2026-11-11 (Nov 11 2026 is a Wednesday, consistent with Opened 15:11 PT); the Lock Pages in Memory / September workaround paragraph matches the article's closing paragraph. OTHER MICROSOFT PAGES NOT OPENED BY THE WRITER: the guessed URLs 404, but the pages exist at other URLs and I read them live: Windows 11 23H2 (status-windows-11-23h2, KB5126653), Windows 10 1607 and Windows Server 2016 (status-windows-10-1607-and-windows-server-2016, KB5126868), Windows Server 2012 R2 (status-windows-8.1-and-windows-server-2012-r2, KB5126836); each lists the issue as Confirmed, Last updated 2026-11-11 15:37 PT, the same next-steps text and the same 12-platform list without 26H2. They do not change the headline claim (they reinforce that 26H2 is the only page listing itself) but the article's 'differ' framing and per-release mapping omit them - filed as a clarification. Windows 10 22H2 page does not carry the issue. Independence: The Register and BleepingComputer are two independent outlets (not required for News). Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic is not a subject of the story (the only Anthropic mention is an unrelated Register sidebar headline), and no Claude/Anthropic credit line appears. Allowlist: learn.microsoft.com, theregister.com and bleepingcomputer.com are all on config/source_allowlist.txt; no additions.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Claim-accuracy tests run: (1) absence/quantifier grep: 'None of the cited sources says...' sentences checked against all 10 snapshots - none gives an out-of-band release date, an installation count, or an explanation of the 26H2 difference (true). 'both reported ... on 2026-11-12' true (Register 12:06 UTC, BleepingComputer Nov 12). 'All eight list 2026-10-13' true. 'Seven other pages ... Last updated 2026-11-11, 15:37 PT' true. (2) Headline/summary/lead keep qualifiers ('might', 'among those known'), do not rename actor or object; the summary says 'The Register differs from a Microsoft page on 26H2', which is accurate. The lead says the update trigger is 'after Windows updates ... are installed' without 'on server devices'; Microsoft's text says 'installed on server devices', which the article itself quotes and discusses in its last-but-one section, so no correction. (3) Dates: calendar dates and PT/UTC basis stated; 12:06 UTC -> 04:06 PT recomputed correctly. (4) Derived figures: 13 vs 12 platforms (7+6 vs 6+6) recomputed, correct; KB mapping correct; vendor figures labelled. (5) Disagreement: reported with attribution to both; no source reconciles it; timing context is the only missing element. (6) Independence recounted: two independent outlets plus Microsoft's own pages. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and precise; explicitly declines to reconcile the Register/Microsoft difference and labels the Herald's own readings as such.
editor_notes.originality: No existing Herald article on the October 2026 Windows updates, KB5126646 or SQL Server linked-server connections (grep of src/content/articles). New topic; no related_articles curated.
concerns: The 'Sources Differ' framing leaves implicit that the 26H2 entry (Last updated 2026-11-12 10:50 PT) was updated 6h44m after the Register published (04:06 PT); filed as a clarification rather than a correction because the article states both timestamps and truthfully says no source explains the difference.

The Windows 11 23H2, Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2012 R2 pages exist at URLs other than the writer's guesses and agree with the seven pages that omit 26H2; the article disclosed it had not opened them.
recommendations: When a guessed learn.microsoft.com release-health URL returns 404, find the real page from the release-health index or search before concluding it cannot be opened.
When a vendor page's last-updated time falls after a news report, state the interval and what it does and does not show.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully qualified vendor-bulletin coverage; headline, summary and lead each verified against raw page text, and the live pages re-checked and unchanged. Published with one clarification covering the 26H2 timing context and three unopened Microsoft pages. Featured candidacy: 1 - confirmed Microsoft known issue with a promised fix, solid for Windows and SQL Server administrators but a narrow audience and not an exceptional story
